narrative.title: Ranking the NOC's Loudest Event Codes
narrative.scenario: A network operations center triages a feed where every event is a single-character code, and by the end of a shift some codes have fired far more often than others. The digest printer re-emits the whole feed rearranged so the noisiest codes lead, repeating each code once per occurrence. Codes tied at the same frequency may land in any order — only the ranking is contractual.
narrative.outputFormat: A rearrangement of s in which every character's block is no shorter than the block of any character that follows it; ties may be ordered arbitrarily.
constraints: s consists of uppercase and lowercase English letters (case matters: 'A' and 'a' are different characters)

testCases.explanation: e occurs twice so both e's lead; the once-occurring letters follow in either order.
Two codes tie at three occurrences, so either block may lead — the stored answer keeps the c block first.

hintLevels: Level 1: The output uses exactly the input's characters — only the emission order changes, driven by how often each one occurs.
Level 2: Tally every character first, then walk the tally from most to least frequent, repeating each character once per occurrence.
Level 3: Ties carry no contractual order, so a fixed tie-break (say, by character value) keeps results deterministic — and remember case-sensitive tallies: 'A' and 'a' count separately.
